sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Straight Swords** are a type of melee armament in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
They boast decently quick attack speeds, with reasonable range and area coverage for said speed. Their movesets are consistently very versatile and easy to use, particularly when one-handed and dual-wielded. Two-handing may be slightly less reliable compared to the other ways of using them, but its increased poise-damage still gives it uses in certain situations.

Overall straight swords pair exceptionally well with shields and most other weapon classes in general, as their regular attack's wide and fast horizontal swings help cover for potential shortcomings that other weapon movesets might face.

They also have exclusive access to the Ash of War: Square Off, a strong and versatile stance skill that easily breaks open blocks with its light attack version and that quickly breaks enemy Stance with its heavy attack version, leaving even bosses open for a Critical Attack within 2 or 3 hits.

sections.heading: Moveset
sections.markdown:
The moveset mostly consists of slashes, with thrusts on every odd one-handed heavy attack, light rolling attack, every third dual wield attack, and dual wield backstep attacks.

It's important to know when to use one-handed or two-handed light attacks, as the one-handed ones wide, horizontal swings makes catching evasive foes or hitting multiple ones easier, while the two-handed ones more vertical approach lets them hit slightly above the wielder and are much easier to use in close environments where other attacks might bounce off walls.

Some straight swords have different standing heavy attacks: the Short Sword always makes thrusts instead of alternating between thrusts and slashes, the Broadsword and Cane Sword has only slashes on their heavy attacks (and their rolling light attack, which most notably also comes out slightly quicker than normal), the Warhawk's Talon that hits twice with its first heavy attack (both the first and second if charged), the Lazuli Glintstone Sword and Carian Knight's Sword both can block when making or charging their heavy attack in exchange for weaker Stance damage, and the Miquellan Knight's Sword has a dashing slash which goes further when charged.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Stray dogs** are enemies in Elden Ring. They tend to gather around groups of humanoids throughout the world of Elden Ring, adding some challenge to certain encounters.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
Strays, like normal canines, often acompany humanoids or form packs. They could potentially be victims of Scarlet rot (Their appearance and prominence in Caelid being a clue) or some form of neglect or extreme metabolism. They are almost always eating some kind of corpse, and are incredibly hostile to the tarnished.

Nonetheless, they have managed to make appearances from Limgrave to Castle Sol being a more common enemy among others. They more than likely serve the same purpose as regular dogs, serving as protectors, companions (of enemies), or both.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.markdown:
Strays (Often just called "Dogs") are canine-like enemies with fast attacks but poor health. They often appear to be either incredibly malnourished or decomposing, often found in Caelid and Crumbling Farum Azula (This "Rotting" appearance is similar to Giant Dogs, perhaps a relation between the two.) They have two major variants, the Stray and the more appealing Noble variant, Although the only major differences are stats and appearance. Two more uncommon variants would be the Bloodied, and Messmer Fire variants.

Their attack patterns can be quite deadly in groups, incredibly fast and punishing if you don't deal with them quickly. They share some similarities to many Wolf variants.

sections.heading: Locations
sections.markdown:
Stray dogs are found throughout the Lands Between and the Realm of Shadow, often near human dwellings.

Otherwise they are often found in these areas;

- Caelid
- Crumbling Farum Azula
- Forbidden Lands (Entrance Area and further)
- Altus Plateau/ Leyndell (Both ashen and regular)
- Limgrave
- MountainTops of the Giants. (Castle Sol, otherwise spread out.)
- Consecrated Snowfield

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
Stray's are almost always consuming something, before being interrupted by hostiles or the tarnished. They almost never can be found just wandering.

Despite their grotesque appearance Stray's have strangely normal sounds, easily recognizable despite their condition.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown:
Strength** is one of the main attribute stats in Elden Ring.

The Tarnished's Strength stat affects which weapons they can wield effectively and affects the damage output of weapons which have Strength scaling. In addition, leveling Strength will also increase the Tarnished's Physical Defense.

The Tarnished can level Strength by spending Runes at Sites of Grace. Strength has soft caps for raising Physical Defense at 30, 40 and 60 points. Soft caps for Strength scaling weapons varies by weapon type and affinities.

When two-handing a weapon Strength is increased by 50%, rounded up, for the purpose of scaling and meeting weapon requirements. A partial exception to this is paired weapons, such as all Fists and Claws, and the Ornamental Straight Sword, who will not get the boost to scaling. The Starscourge Greatsword, however, still receives the Strength bonus in spite of being a paired weapon.

Note that this Strength-boost also can be applied to Incantations via the Clawmark Seal, but that it doesn't apply to skills with a separate "bullet" attack that scales with Strength, such as Flame of the Redmanes, Ground Slam, or Storm Blade.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown:
Sorceries** (魔術, *Majutsu*) are a medium of spells in Elden Ring.

All sorceries require some FP to be cast and the majority of them require a heavy investment into the Intelligence stat, however, there are still some Faith and Arcane-based sorceries to be found. Sorceries can only be manifested through the use of Staves acting as a catalyst.

The actual damage or effect per casting of a Sorcery is based on a unique stat of Staves called Sorcery Scaling, or SS. The value of this stat for any staff depends on the quality of the staff, its Strengthening level, and a combination of your relevant Stats and Attributes combined with the staff's Grade Ratio for those attributes (primarily focusing on Intelligence). Individual spells will have their Power ratio represented as % SS (such as POWER: 75% SS), which represents the percentage of an equipped staff's Sorcery Scaling value that is used for each shot. Do note that enemy resistances will factor into how much damage you see an enemy take; the Power % shown for attack spells is based on calculations done on unarmored neutral critters in the starting zones.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: St. Trina**, also known as the **saint of sleep**, is an NPC character in Elden Ring: Shadow of the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.markdown:
A pale young girl, delicately swaddled within the nurturing petals of a motherly deep-purple flower, rests her cherubic head on folded arms as she slumbers within her tranquil garden. Purple blood seeps from an unhealed wound on the left side of St. Trina's head, and her plant-like lower body twists into a dark stalk that roots her to the earth. A silvery-white streak graces her flowing purple hair, and the sweet, poisonous nectar she secretes grants eternal rest to those who partake of it.

Her earlier form was that of an alluring young woman with two long braids, yet her destined adult form was considered unsettling. Crowned by a flower with eight petals, this cyclopean deity was expected to a awaken a third eye and eight wild braids of hair that coiled into eddy-like spirals.

sections.heading: Location
sections.markdown: St. Trina is found in a small cave within the Garden of Deep Purple at the bottom of the Stone Coffin Fissure.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
An enigmatic and fleeting individual who held dominion over sleep, some say she is a comely young girl, others are sure he is a boy. The only certainty is that their appearance was as sudden as their disappearance. She was the other half of Miquella, the aspect of his love thanks to his Empyrean nature. The Empyrean and aspect inhabit the same body, much like Queen Marika and Lord Radagon. As Miquella they appeared a small, golden-haired boy; as Trina, a prepossessing young woman with silver, light-purple hair.

St. Trina's love was boundless, offering gentle, intoxicating rest to those she visited in dreams. Some inhabitants of the Lands Between were so enamored that they formed a cult. Light-purple water lilies on the verge of wilting numbed the senses and prevented agitation, symbolizing faith in Trina. Seeking to find her again in their sleep, Trina's followers developed poisonous concoctions to elicit deeper slumber, and some priests were rumored to use sleep-inducing arrows for ritual purposes. Dolores the Sleeping Arrow and Thiollier were among her greatest devotees.

In the final act of the Shattering, Miquella and Malenia mustered an army of Cleanrot Knights and departed the Haligtree for Caelid to confront General Radahn regarding the vow. The ensuing Battle of Aeonia culminated in a duel between Radahn and Malenia, who snapped Miquella's Needle to break the stalemate, unleashing her first scarlet rot bloom. Although she gained wings of strength, fierce Malenia, Blade of Miquella, soon fell into a deep slumber.

During Miquella's pilgrimage through the Realm of Shadow, he stopped at the Cerulean Coast and traveled downward into the Stone Coffin Fissure. Deep underground, the Empyrean stood atop the largest stone coffin and divested himself of his love and adoring other self, casting Trina into the chasm's darkest depths. Liberated from his fate and eternal childhood, he sealed the Fissure and resumed his injurious path to godhood.

St. Trina survived her fall; wounded, flowers burgeoned where her nectar-like blood pooled. Her faint, light-purple slumber mists concentrated into an intoxicating deep-purple fog. Trina blossomed, manifesting deep-purple water lilies and forming her Garden of Deep Purple. The congealed, arcane putrescence of ancient heroes imbibed her poisonous nectar, received velvety eternal rest, and became her gallant Putrescent Knight.

Trina's love for Miquella never wavered, even after her abandonment. Unable to speak directly, her singular wish was to grant Miquella forgiveness in death, knowing that godhood would become his prison. If her wish is granted, Trina withers and dies, leaving behind a single harmless water lily.

- The path to Trina is protected by * Bloodfiends, Gravebirds, Sentry Stones, and Putrescent Skeletons. In addition to his seal, Miquella left behind the golden spirit of a Misbegotten Warrior.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown:
- *Trina* is a feminine inflection of the Latin *trīnus* ("three" or "triple"), affirming her status as a triplet.
- The unmarked location in Altus Plateau where the Amber Starlight is found is internally referred to as "St. Trina's Hideaway", and features a statue of Miquella and his twin, Malenia.
- An additional voiceline was cut from *Shadow of the Erdtree*. If the player visited Trina and drank her nectar after defeating Promised Consort Radahn she would have thanked the player for their deed before finally withering.
- Several early iterations of St. Trina were cut from *Elden Ring* during development.
 - In the files, **St. Trina of the Cradlesong** sang a lullaby to the Nomadic Merchants, granting them succour by alleviating the Frenzied Flame and allowing them to sleep. After the singer vanished, the merchants left their prison, and soothed themselves by playing the song on their instruments. Later, Merchant Kalé asked the player to collect Slumber Fog with St. Trina's Crystal Ball so he could recreate the effect.
 - In a later version, Reeling Rico used Slumber Fog to produce Dreambrew, an alcoholic potion that revealed secrets. His questline would have concluded at the Cocoon of the Empyrean, where he would have discovered St. Trina was Miquella all along.
 - Intriguingly, the Network Test files lacked Miquella's Lilies to match Trina's Lilies, the Chinese and Korean versions of St. Trina's Torch describes her as active since ancient times, and there is no reference to apparent gender fluidity in Sword of St. Trina, suggesting that her textual connection to Miquella had yet to be implemented at this point of development.
- Quella, a young boy whose emblem was a sacred tree, was the god of dreams in *Dark Souls II*.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
A derelict castle sinking into a poisonous mire in the north of Altus Plateau. For generations, the Shaded Castle was ruled over by House Marais, who served as both executioners and castellans. Maleigh Marais, born sickly like all sons of House Marais, became beguiled by Malenia, claiming to feel her presence when he held the Valkyrie's Prosthesis

Elemer of the Briar, an infamous killer of instructors and merchants, was held in the castle for execution. However, he managed to steal the executioner's sword of House Marais and furnished it with the battle skills of his home of Eochaid, thus avoiding execution. Elemer succeeded in taking over the castle, bringing about the ruin of House Marais. Maleigh Marais can be found wandering the craggy wasteland to the west of the castle.

An intricate system of sewers and dungeons that spreads out below the capital. The Three Fingers can be met behind a door at the lowest level of the catacomb, provided one removes all of their equipment first.

sections.markdown: Starcaller**s, also known as **Meteorite Scavengers** and **Meteorite Seekers**, are enemies in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
Starcallers are hooded scavengers who search for rocks imbued with gravity magic left behind by meteor strikes. They are commonly found around craters, digging into the earth with crude pickaxes, which double as their primary weapons. Starcallers also utilize Gravity Stone Fans and gravity-infused Ashes of War in combat.

Their attire consists of filthy hooded robes and simple leather shoes. Multi-colored Rainbow Stones are strung like beads along their waists and embedded in their robes, while a sack of loose netting filled with similar stones is slung over their backs and secured with rope. Equipped with their rudimentary pickaxes, the starcallers work tirelessly to harvest fallen stars and the remnants of their power.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
The starcallers were practitioners of gravity-based glintstone sorcery. They traveled to meteor impact sites to harvest rocks imbued with gravitational energy.

After learning gravity sorcery from an Alabaster Lord, Radahn confronted the stars and defended Sellia during the Starscourge Conflict. In the time that followed, falling stars were rare in the Lands Between. For this reason, the starcallers were desperate to scavenge what precious few gravity stone chunks they could find.

sections.markdown:
Sorcery Scaling** is an attack power stat in Elden Ring.

Sorcery Scaling is a stat unique to Glintstone Staves, and increases the amount of damage caused by Sorceries cast by the staff used. The Tarnished must meet the required attribute stats to wield the weapon, or the Sorcery Scaling will be reduced. On the other hand, exceeding the Intelligence requirement will increase the Sorcery Scaling of the staff used. Sorcery Scaling can also be increased by upgrading the Glintstone Staves.

Sorcery Scaling only affects the damage of the spells cast by the staff, and has no effect on the duration of buffs or other sorceries. The Sorcery Scaling of the staff used to attack is the only Sorcery Scaling used to determine the effectiveness of the attack. Having a second staff equipped will not affect Sorcery Scaling on the first staff.

A related and often confused effect is that a very few passive buffs, such as the 30% Gravity Magic damage boost of the Meteor Staff and the 30% damage boost to Invisibility Magic from the Staff of Loss, will apply when the staff with the buff is equipped in the non-casting hand. This increases the damage of the buffed type of magic from the casing staff but does not increase the Sorcery Scaling of the casting staff. The damage buff is applied after the calculation that uses the Sorcery Scaling of the casting staff. This is easily verified by experiment.

sections.heading: Overview

It is a bottomless pit that instantly kills anything that falls into it and is the only one of its kind amongst the surface world of the Lands Between, as every other lethal fall is either tied to coastal waters or mountainous cliffs. It can be found in Limgrave, southeast of the First Step Site of Grace.

Notable for its surprisingly high count of fatalities, the pit is visually distinguished by its eleven crucifixes, three breakable carts, and several flying Man-Bats patrolling its surroundings. The main source of its fatalities is caused by the north and western edges of the hole being geographically higher compared to the rest of the surroundings, obscuring its presence to anyone nearby on its north and western sides, the hazard only being made clear when the player gets dangerously close to the edge.

It is possible to exploit this obscurity in PvP. If one player gets another to chase them, they can bait the chasing player to follow them to the northern edges of the hole and then jump across to the southern side. If the chaser is unaware of the hole's geography, they may either jump too early or too late in their attempt to catch up to the running player, causing them to fall down into the hole and die.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: The Heroic Concept** is a design philosophy followed by Hidetaka Miyazaki and the development team at FromSoftware that shapes the characteristics and themes of certain characters found within Elden Ring's story, primarily the Shardbearers in particular.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown: The philosophy places focus on characters carrying noble or heroic aspects that become warped and twisted into something malign due the circumstances they've been placed in. Whether it be an inability to handle the power received from their respective great rune, coping with the trauma of a unfortunate event or their fundamental noble principles getting pushed to such an extreme that it transforms into a vice. Either way the source of their personal downfall usually does not stem far away from their once respectable traits.

sections.heading: *Godrick the Golden*
sections.markdown:
Born a small, frail child amongst his far stronger kin. From his very birth, Godrick was destined for an endless uphill battle for relevancy. From a young age Godrick has beem yearning to prove his worth as a true heir to the Golden Lineage and so he would pursue great varieties of ways to improve himself and his lordsworn army.

However his primary manner of bolstering himself would quickly devolve into piteous scavenging for old relics and stealing and grafting body parts of less fortunate people and creatures alike on to himself and his closest assets.

sections.heading: *Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon*
sections.markdown:
Once a great Carian queen who led a military that could resist the (at the time) unstoppable armies of the Golden Order. Queen Rennala was intelligent, strong, beautiful and certainly not least, loving.

Her unmatched love would be her downfall though, as Radagon's departure would leave her broken from grief, her unconditional love and dedication to the frail, transient Juvenile Scholars entrapping her within the Grand Library.

sections.heading: *General Radahn*
sections.markdown:
In his prime, General Radahn was one of the most powerful demigods in the Lands Between, being equally matched in combat against his half-sister Malenia. Most importantly, Radahn was known for his charisma, skill and intelligence in military leadership and battle. Being a noble commander of honor, he inspired confidence in and valued his Redmane soldiers and Knights, which is what earned him their respect in the first place.

However, during the Shattering, the great power of his Great Rune alongside the other Great Runes of the other Shardbearers, drove him to go to war against his fellow kin. This would eventually lead to a battle against Malenia, which ultimately ended in a stalemate when Malenia unleashed her Scarlet Rot, which drove Radahn to madness, turning into a mindless and feral beast who would feast on the corpses of both friends and foes alike.

sections.heading: *Praetor Rykard*
sections.markdown:
Once a ruthless justiciar who led an army of inquisitors to ruthlessly hunt and torture heretics, Praetor Rykard descended into blasphemy following the discovery of ancient spells of a long-forgotten snake-worshipping religion on Mt. Gelmir. His increasingly heretic tendencies led him to assist his sister Ranni in the Night of Black Knives, in which Godwyn the Golden was assassinated.

During the Shattering, he became strongly disillusioned with the Erdtree and the Golden Order, finding that the Gods demanding the demigods to fight over the Great Runes (whom he refers to as "miserly scraps of power") as nothing but debasing. Thus, he launched a blasphemous campaign against the Golden Order, establishing the rule of taking by force and the belief that the Gods are no different.

Despite his heresy, many followers were drawn by his ambition, as they also became disillusioned with the Golden Order, and they came to see Rykard's intentions as noble. They then waged war against the armies of Leyndell in Rykard's name, though the results were costly and appalling.

Praetor Rykard eventually lost his sanity and fed himself to the Blasphemous/God-devouring serpent, merging himself with the creature. With his ambition descending into gluttonous depravity, the now-monstrous Rykard began engaging in cannibalism, where he would devour his greatest champions, thus making them a part of his "family".

sections.heading: *Morgott, the Omen King*
sections.markdown:
Born an Omen, Morgott came to renounce his accursed blood and would seal it away within a blade, which was then concealed within his wooden staff. Following Queen Marika's shattering of the Elden Ring, Morgott secured power over Leyndell, Royal Capital and devoted himself to protecting the capital and the Erdtree from his other siblings, as he considers them traitors to the Golden Order for going against it in favor of their own ambitions.

Despite his deeds, unfortunately, they weren't recognized by many even the Golden Order, who reviled as an accursed fiend. Despite this, Morgott remained steadfastly loyal, as he considers loyalty to be a reward in its own right, and despite knowing that the Erdtree wouldn't admit anyone, not even himself, to claim the title of Elden Lord. However, his devotion and loyalty towards the Golden Order proved to be his downfall as he met defeat at the hands of a Tarnished of no renown.

sections.heading: *Mohg, Lord of Blood*
sections.markdown:
Like his brother Morgott, Mohg was accursed at birth. Unlike the former, who renounced his Omen blood, Mohg came to embrace it. After an encounter with an Outer God known as the Formless Mother, he established a cult, where he and his followers would perform blood-associated rituals as her servants. Seeking to become Elden Lord, and while recruiting and kidnapping many followers to his cause, Mohg plots to overthrow the Golden Order in favor of his own dynasty, which he calls the Mohgwyn Dynasty.

As he has a strong obsession of his half-brother Miquella, Mohg believes the young Empyrean has the potential of ascending to Godhood, he plans to make him his puppet and rule alongside him as his consort. And so he abducts Miquella from the Haligtree to have him facilitated with blood for his awakening. However, no matter how hard Mohg tried to interact with him, the slumbering Miquella never responded.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown:
Smoldering Walls** are perpetually burning stone walls found throughout Caelid. Constructed by the Redmanes after the Battle of Aeonia in an effort to suppress the spread of the Scarlet Rot.

They are lined in several layers throughout the land, with several walls barricading the entrances to Fort Gael and Redmane Castle. One extremely long wall can be found crossing the entire midsection of the western countryside and across the southern edges of Greyoll's Dragonbarrow. Another smaller wall found west of Rotview Balcony, marking the border between Limgrave and Caelid and acting as an ominous warning to outsiders of the dangers lurking within the rot-infested land.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown: - It's possible the Smoldering Church was originally set ablaze to act as an additional means of slowing down the spread of the rot.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: The **Guilty**, also known as **exiled criminals**, are a faction in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown: The Guilty are convicted criminals of the Lands Between. They are often punished through crucifixion, imprisonment, exile, execution and most iconic of all, marked with briars that coil around their bodies, many having their eyes gouged out by their razor-sharp thorns. Several of these blinded subjects eventually discovered the blood star as they lived in their eternal darkness.

sections.heading: The Crucified
sections.markdown:
Crucified subjects can be found all over the Lands Between, though most notably in Limgrave and Altus Plateau. Mimicking the subjugation of Queen Marika, they have their hands nailed to a wooden board in the shape of a Rune Arc for an undisclosed (if not infinite) amount of time. They usually either wear a simple plain garb and trousers along with a hood with a collar made of sharpened branches. Or no clothes at all, their bodies visibly burned and charred. The former being sentenced for lesser, petty crimes and the latter likely for more severe indictments. Queen Marika has also been sentenced to this punishment, though she has been strung up to an actual, enormous rune arc.

The crucified of Limgrave are completely inert during daytime, but spring to life with horrific cries of pain and agony during the night.

While the crucifixes near Dominula don't have anyone hanging on them, they have been uniquely decorated with pink flowers by the local inhabitants. Due to their allegiance to the local Godskin Apostle it's likely done in mockery of the Queen's image and and may serve as a celebration of her suffering.

sections.heading: Briars of Sin
sections.markdown:
While briars are used as a means of punishment conducted by a figure of authority. They do curiously seem to appear on their own in environments inhabited by either a great number of criminals or by a single criminal convicted of a particularly heinous sin.

Notable locations infested by briars include:
- Stormveil Castle, with it's myriad of Exile Soldiers and Banished Knights likely serving as their penal colony with it's location at the fringes of the Lands Between.
- Flame Peak with it's graveyard of fallen Fire Giants and serving as the site that would allow for the commitment of the Golden Order's first cardinal sin, the burning of the Erdtree.
- The entrance of the Erdtree itself, which serves as the prison of Queen Marika for her crime of shattering the Elden Ring.

sections.heading: The Blood Star
sections.markdown: An unknown entity perceived by those blinded by thorns. It's powers appears to manifest in the form of bloodthorn sorceries and the creation of red glintstone through the blood of sacrifices, allowing staves infused with such stones to scale with one's Faith at the complete abandonment of Intelligence. Earning its practitioners of Aberrant Sorceries the ire of the academy scholars as well.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Stormveil** was a faction mentioned in Elden Ring. Not to be confused with the stronghold of the same name, the members of Stormveil were the ancient, original inhabitants and operators of Stormveil Castle. Known for the development of their unique storm-based battle arts, channeling the power of the ceaseless winds that encircled their home.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
, before receiving its current decor]]
Long ago, when Stormveil's winds were unmatched, its people allied with mighty Stormhawks—formidable warriors shaped by the raging cyclones around them. The cries of their strongest hawks emboldened comrades in battle, while the winds they carried could tear through foes. The faction was led by the proud and revered Stormhawk King and later by the Storm Lord, though these entities may be the same. From their fortress on Stormhill, they oversaw all of Limgrave and the Weeping Peninsula.

During the Age of the Erdtree, the armies of the Golden Order attacked Stormveil. The Storm Lord was ultimately defeated in solo combat by Lord Godfrey. Stormveil Castle was later claimed by the Golden Order and repurposed as a penal colony for Exile Soldiers and Banished Knights. These outcasts attempted to continue the castle's traditions, but lacked the skill of its original masters. Their stormhawks and even the castle's surrounding winds weakened over time. Unable to train the birds in storm arts, they resorted to grafting weapons onto them—a practice that killed many.

The castle's condition worsened further under the rule of Godrick the Grafted.

Nepheli Loux, Warrior can claim the title of Lord of Limgrave.

sections.markdown: Spirit eels** are wildlife enemies in Shadow of the Erdtree. They are mostly passive creatures that behave similarly to spirit jellyfish, turning red when provoked.

There is a variant that looks like an inflated balloon. When aggressors come too close, it expands and explodes.

sections.markdown:
Found in a treasure chest in the western Ancient Ruins.

If you have the Ancient Ruins, Grand Stairway Site of Grace unlocked, start there and take the nearby lift down; then, enter the square passage towards the south by using Torrent's double jump, using the adjacent pile of rocks to gain enough height to do so. If you only have the Rauh Ancient Ruins, West grace unlocked, start there and enter the tunnel to the southwest. Follow the tunnel's left wall until you reach a lift; take it up and then round the corner to the left. Below the cliff is a walkable lattice structure; jump down onto it and follow the path. At the intersection, enter the room to your left, which contains the aforementioned square passage and the elevator to the Grand Stairway grace.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown:
Somber Smithing Stones** (also simply known as *Somberstones*) are Bolstering Materials in Elden Ring, of which 10 variants exist. They are rarer counterparts of ordinary Smithing Stones required for upgrading certain special Weapons.

They can be used by Smithing Master Hewg or War Counselor Iji to incrementally upgrade such special Weapons in exchange for runes, up to +10, consuming one stone in the process. Each "tier" of Somber Smithing Stone can upgrade an armament once, to the same level as the number in their name. Somber Ancient Dragon Smithing Stones are the sole exception to this naming scheme, being the equivalent of a Somber Smithing Stone 10.

However, for ordinary armaments, regular Smithing Stones are needed instead; such armaments can be upgraded all the way to +25, and require 12 stones per 3 upgrades, except for the final one which only requires 1 Ancient Dragon Smithing Stone.

They can be found scattered through both the Lands Between and the Realm of Shadow, sometimes looted from certain enemies when killed, or purchased from some Merchants in usually limited quantity. However, excepting Somber Ancient Dragon Smithing Stones, they can be purchased in unlimited quantity from the Twin Maiden Husks after giving them Somberstone Miner's Bell Bearings, of which 4 are scattered throughout the Lands Between.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: The **Sword of Darkness** is a melee armament in Elden Ring, included in the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.markdown:
- Take the Stone-Sheathed Sword or Sword of Light to an altar at either Fog Rift Catacombs or Ruins of Unte.
 - **WARNING** : Once either the Sword of Darkness or Sword of Light has been acquired, though the two forms can be freely switched between by traveling to their assigned altars, the Stone-Sheathed Sword itself cannot be reacquired until you enter the next new game cycle.
 - See the page for the Stone-Sheathed Sword for all 3 altar locations.
 - If the Stone-Sheathed Sword was taken from Fog Rift Catacombs or Ancient Ruins of Rauh, the altar at Ruins of Unte should be used. If it was taken from Ruins of Unte, the altar at Fog Rift Catacombs should be used.

sections.heading: Upgrade Information
sections.markdown:
- Upgraded with Somber Smithing Stones.
- Cannot have its Affinity and Skill changed.
- The upper number in the Atk column denotes Physical base damage while the lower, colored number in the Atk column denotes elemental base damage: red for Fire damage, yellow for Lightning damage, orange for Holy damage, and cyan for Magic damage.
- See the Weapon Scaling page for what the scaling values mean.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- The unique skill, Darkness, sprays streams of Holy darkness in a rotating circle around the user. This takes about 4 seconds to cast and reduces the Holy damage negation for any enemies hit by 20% for 60 seconds. Since this casts quite slowly, taking about 4 seconds to complete, it's best used in an ambush to strengthen any Holy damage attacks used afterwards.
 - The debuff inflicted does not stack with any other defence or attack debuff, except Frostbite. This includes the two moon sorceries Rennala's Full Moon and Ranni's Dark Moon, the Shriek of Milos of the Sword of Milos, Acid Spraymist, and the Soul Stifler skill of the Winged Greathorn.
 - Since the Sword of Light's skill, Light, works as a Body Buff, these two skills work well together to raise the damage of Holy attacks significantly.
- Has identical statistics to the Sword of Light. Only their unique skills and appearances distinguish one from the other.
- A single sword switched between Sword of Darkness, Sword of Light, and Stone-Sheathed Sword forms always has the same level.
 - This means that if the Stone-Sheathed Sword is upgraded to +3 before switching to Sword of Darkness, you will gain a Sword of Darkness +3. If it's then upgraded to +7 it will become a Sword of Light +7 when switched.
- Incredibly bad damage negation when blocking, even for a Straight Sword.
- Note that all swords currently held in one's inventory switch forms when the respective altar is interacted with. Thus, keeping one sword in the item box allows for the dual-wielding of the Sword of Darkness and Sword of Light.
- Scales the best with a pure Strength build but due to scaling becoming less effective when stats are leveled above 54 a hybrid Strength/Faith build performs almost as well. The second, hybrid build will also deal more damage with the skill.
 - For comparison (unmentioned stats are at the minimum required level): 80 Strength grants 638 Attack Power (AP), and 45 Strength and 45 Faith grants 622 AP.
 - Note that the high levels of Faith required to wield the sword, a hybrid Strength/Faith build, effectively have 14 more levels to work with. These could either be put in other stats, such as Endurance for more Equip Load or Stamina, or Mind for more FP, but they could also be put into Strength and Faith for more AP. Doing this would put both stats at 52 and grant 642 AP.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: The **Stone-Sheathed Sword** is a melee armament in *Elden Ring: Shadow of the Erdtree*.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.markdown:
- Found at an altar in either Fog Rift Catacombs, Ruins of Unte, or Ancient Ruins of Rauh. Since the altar in Fog Rift Catacombs is the most complicated to reach, it's recommended that the sword be taken there so that the later interactions with altars are less time-consuming.
 - **WARNING** : Once either the Sword of Darkness or Sword of Light has been acquired, though the two forms can be freely switched between by traveling to their assigned altars, the Stone-Sheathed Sword itself cannot be reacquired until you enter the next new game cycle.
 - Fog Rift Catacombs: From the start, follow the path so that you pass the first and second falling-spikes roofs to the elevator. Continue to the third falling-spikes roof and get to the other side of the room (be wary of the pit in the second saferoom to the left). Use the raised platform at the end of the room to enter the hidden compartment in the falling roof, then ride it to a higher platform so you can stand on top of the falling roof. The altar is in the opposite right corner of the room, on the roof.
 - Picking the sword up here means it turns into the Sword of Darkness at Ruins of Unte and the Sword of Light at Ancient Ruins of Rauh.
 - Ruins of Unte: Found to the right inside the courtyard, blocked by a Furnace Golem (a Hefty Fire Pot can get it going again to open the path).
 - Picking the sword up here means it turns into the Sword of Darkness at Fog Rift Catacombs and the Sword of Light at Ancient Ruins of Rauh.
 - Ancient Ruins of Rauh: From Ancient Rauh Ruins, East Site of Grace, head across the bridge towards the west, then continue forward until a small body of water, and take a right. Take the Spirit Spring that is now straight ahead and jump forward (north-northeast on the map) to a ruin underneath the large cliff. Here is a body with the Greater Potentate's Cookbook 9 on a pile of rubble. Standing at the cookbook with the Spirit Spring directly behind you, turn to the right to see a tower and a "broken" bridge (actually just invisible) that can be crossed to reach the altar.
 - Picking the sword up here means it turns into the Sword of Darkness at Ruins of Unte and the Sword of Light at Fog Rift Catacombs.

sections.heading: Upgrade Information
sections.markdown:
- Upgraded with Somber Smithing Stones.
- Cannot have its Affinity and Skill changed.
- See the Weapon Scaling page for what the scaling values mean.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- While the locked skill, Square Off, is rather generic for a Straight Sword, it's still powerful due to the guard-breaking ability of its light attack version and the heavy Stance-breaking of its heavy attack version.
- A single sword switched between Sword of Darkness, Sword of Light, and Stone-Sheathed Sword forms always has the same level.
 - This means that if the Stone-Sheathed Sword is upgraded to +3 before switching to Sword of Darkness, you will gain a Sword of Darkness +3. If it's then upgraded to +7, it will become a Sword of Light +7 when switched.
- Note that all swords currently held in one's inventory switch forms when the respective altar is interacted with. Thus, extra Stone-Sheathed Swords should be kept in the item box when interacting with the altars to switch between the Sword of Light and Sword of Darkness forms.
- There are a few reasons to keep the sword in this form, as it's a fairly weak weapon that is only barely stronger than the Cane Sword.
 - It has one interesting quality, which is that it's a Straight Sword that inflicts Strike damage, which is strong against mechanical, armored, and skeletal foes.
 - Its scaling is quite different from the Sword of Light and Sword of Darkness, with its Strength-scaling at +0 completely outstripping either other sword's Strength-scaling at +10, and its Dexterity-scaling also almost does the same, and it has no Faith requirement. In exchange, its Physical damage is lower, and it completely lacks Holy damage and Faith-scaling.
- Though this weapon technically gains the most Attack Power (AP) from a pure Strength build, a hybrid Strength/Dexterity build with a leaning towards Strength works better since it barely sacrifices one-handed Attack Power in exchange for a slightly greater amount of Attack Power when two-handed.
 - For comparison (unmentioned stats are at the minimum required level): 80 Strength grants 459 AP, 60 Strength and 30 Dexterity grants 458 AP, and 45 Strength and 45 Dexterity grants 443 AP. Two-handing grants 488 AP, 503 AP, and 493 AP, respectively.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: , also known as **coffin-ships**, are objects in Shadow of the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.markdown:
Stone coffins are monolithic vessels that resemble arks, identified by their prominent bull figureheads. They feature abundant carvings of people, trees, birds, beasts, and snakes. Engravings along the hull portray a procession of pallbearers seemingly bearing the weight of the main deck. The coffin interior features hallways lined with columns, but the center is completely solid. Bearded Ancient Dynasty Statues, clutching a tablet, are found on and within the stone coffins. His beard is notably smaller here and he lacks his usual roots.

They contain column-lined, functional hallways, though their cores are completely solid. Some coffins are embedded in the earth in a way that gives the impression the surrounding rock solidified around them.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
The massive stone coffins housed the putrescent remains of impure individuals, who were sent off with Great Grave Glovewort as part of their burial rites. Resembling colossal arks, these coffins are decorated with sculptures of bulls, beasts, and the bearded, tablet-clutching man of the Ancient Dynasty. They washed ashore on the Cerulean Coast, arriving in the Lands Between long ago when Death was still burned with the cold ghostflame. The tainted flesh had putrified into a foul liquor that nonetheless received the cleansing Death rites of the time.

Over time, the coffins accumulated in the Stone Coffin Fissure and their leaked contents pooled in the Garden of Deep Purple. After St. Trina was abandoned by Miquella the Kind during his pilgrimage through the Realm of Shadow, the sludge imbibed her nectar, received its long sought-after eternal rest, and coalesced into her Putrescent Knight.

sections.heading: Locations
sections.markdown: Stone coffins are found only in the Realm of Shadow along the Cerulean Coast and inside the Stone Coffin Fissure. A few nearly touch the adjacent Charo's Hidden Grave.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Miquella cast St. Trina from the bow of the largest stone coffin, found at the Fissure Depths.
- Stone coffins appear in the art of ancient cultures.
 - The arrival of stone coffins marked the beginning of the Ancient Dynasty, as recorded on the beacon obelisks found in the Hallowhorn Grounds along the Siofra River. These must be lit with fire to commune with Ancestor Spirits.
 - A boat decoration in Enir-Ilim includes a funeral procession and twin horned figureheads, though the beasts are goats instead of bulls.
- Grave Crickets are drawn to the stone coffins.
- Demi-Human Queen Marigga is located beside a beached stone coffin.
- The coffins inside the Stone Coffin Fissure are guarded by Sentry Stones that fire energy beams and Gravebirds with soporific powers.
- Claymen most likely came from stone coffins because their Japanese name ("Mud People") corresponds with its term for Putrescent Knight ("Mud Knight"), though it's unclear whether they formed from existing putrescence or putrified over many ages.

Sporting blue-green feathers, teal eyes, and magnificently shining crests, Spectral Hawks are large bird spirits that fly the Nightfarers to the land of Limveld at the start of each Expedition. sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: The **Stone Coffin Fissure** (石棺の大穴, *Sekkan no Ooana*) is a legacy dungeon located within the Realm of Shadow in Shadow of the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
Stone Coffin Fissure is a vast chasm beneath the Southern Shore, filled with countless stone coffins and enemies that inflict Sleep ailment buildup. This dungeon is linear and its primary boss is the Putrescent Knight.

The dungeon's entrance is a gaping pit on a peninsula along the Cerulean Coast, at the southernmost tip of the Realm of Shadow. The The Fissure site of grace lies just below the surface, outside the dungeon. Initially, a Haligtree seal blocks access, breaking only when Miquella discards his Great Rune. This event is triggered when the Tarnished approaches the Shadow Keep or crosses the bridge east of Bonny Village heading north.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
The Stone Coffin Fissure accumulated many stone coffins over the ages. In ancient times, ghostflame cleansed the impure lives within these vessels, but their putrid remains eventually congealed into Putrescence.

After the Shattering, the Empyrean Miquella embarked on a self-sacrificial pilgrimage to the Land of Shadow to attone for the sins of his mother, Queen Marika the Eternal. Before his ascension to godhood, Miquella attempted to rid himself of his curse of nascency by casting off his other self, St. Trina, into the chasm. In doing so, he abandoned his ability to love, dooming his Age of Compassion.

At the bottom of the fissure, St. Trina's slumbering presence transformed the land into the Garden of Deep Purple, where Deep-Purple Lilies and Nectarblood Burgeon began to bloom. The leaking contents of the stone coffins imbibed her velvety nectar, achieving eternal rest and manifesting as the Putrescent Knight.

Loot**: Rabbath's Rise

sections.heading: Use

- Blue glintstone crystals grow on this blue-green bell bearing.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Spiritgraves** are a concept in Elden Ring, introduced in the Shadow of the Erdtree DLC.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.markdown: Spiritgraves are spectral grave markers with a ghostly white glow.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown: Gravestones on the Gravesite Plain eventually turned into spirits, the oldest of which have faded away entirely. Under rare circumstances, they sprout short-lived Larval Tears that are neither flesh nor spirit, but something in between. Stone Gravebirds were constructed in ancient times to protect the spiritgraves.

sections.heading: Locations
sections.markdown:
- Gravesite Plain
- Rauh Base
- Scadu Altus

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Ancestral Followers believe new life will also sprout from their souls.
- Spiritgrave Stones are a Crafting Material for Polter Stones, Sunwarmth Stones, and Surging Frenzied Flames.
- Seeds from Rada Fruit grow into wheat-like spiritgrave grass.
